assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints turn small shocks into persistent, amplified credit cycles. The mechanism rests on a financial-contracting friction, and it became a workhorse for the macro-finance literature after 2008. It is conceptually foundational and has had wide influence on research and policy.
assessment.attribution: The core idea is clearly the two-author Kiyotaki-Moore contribution. Gertler, Gilchrist and the financial-accelerator literature built a closely related line, but that line is partly recognised by the 2022 prize to Bernanke. Restricting the award to Kiyotaki and Moore is the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of confirmation, extension and use in policy models. Post-crisis empirical and quantitative work has validated the mechanism's relevance.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Gertler or Gilchrist, given overlap with the Bernanke-related prize.
Direct empirical identification of the original amplification mechanism is more mixed than its theoretical influence suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and the Woodford synthesis of the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice worldwide. Impact on both theory and policy is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is wide (eight names). Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (micro-founded monetary theory) are the clearest conceptual originators. Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets were central to estimation and quantification, so the three-name limit forces hard exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and confirmation. Inflation in 2021-23 tested the framework, with mixed assessments, but the framework is still the dominant paradigm.
uncertainties: Contested attribution among Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Galí and Gertler.
Debate over the framework's performance after the 2021-23 inflation episode.
Macroeconomics has had several recent prizes, which may crowd the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reframed how technology and trade reshape labour demand through tasks, job polarisation and local-labour-market adjustment to import competition. It changed empirical practice and informs political and policy debate. The evidence is high-quality and spans trade, labour and technology.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across tasks and the China shock. Hanson is central to the trade-shock evidence. Katz is central to the earlier skill-premium and technology work. Dorn is a key co-author of the China shock papers but more junior.
assessment.maturity: The task approach has about two decades of confirmation. The China shock results have been replicated and extended, though with ongoing debate about magnitudes.
uncertainties: Selection among four credited names; Katz also appears under another candidate.
Debate over the magnitude and persistence of the China shock effects.
Overlap with the 2024 prize to Acemoglu on technology and institutions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Hsieh-Klenow framework turned misallocation of inputs across firms into a measurable, quantitative explanation for cross-country income gaps. It is a major advance in development and growth economics, widely used in practice and in policy diagnosis.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 Hsieh-Klenow paper is the clear centrepiece. Restuccia (with Rogerson) contributed a parallel, early policy-distortion perspective and is a plausible third name, but the two-author core is the cleaner attribution.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of use and extension. Measurement issues (markup versus distortion, adjustment costs, mismeasurement) remain active.
uncertainties: Whether measured dispersion reflects true distortions or measurement error and unobserved heterogeneity.
Whether the committee would include Restuccia and Rogerson-related precursors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a new area of information economics in which a designer chooses the information structure. It has produced a tractable theory and applications in markets, regulation, politics and platforms. The conceptual advance is clear and extends the information-economics tradition recognised in 1996, 2001 and 2007.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated Bayesian persuasion. Morris and Bergemann developed information design and the related Bayes-correlated-equilibrium approach. Four names are credited, so any three-name selection leaves out a major contributor, and Morris's wider contributions (global games, robust mechanism design) are a further consideration.
assessment.maturity: The theory is about fifteen years old. Applied use is growing but still developing, and empirical confirmation is thin relative to older candidates.
uncertainties: Choice between Morris and Bergemann as the third name.
Limited empirical validation and real-world impact so far.
Possibly early for recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi showed with granular data that household leverage and credit supply expansion drove the housing boom, the bust and the depth of the Great Recession. This created an empirical agenda linking finance and macroeconomics with strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: The contribution is overwhelmingly the Mian-Sufi partnership, so attribution is clean. Campbell is a major household-finance figure whose work is related but distinct.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years old. Findings have been extended internationally, though some interpretations (credit supply versus expectations) remain debated.
uncertainties: Debate over credit-supply versus belief-driven explanations.
Relatively recent compared with the most mature candidates.
Overlap in theme with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical optimal taxation, the sufficient-statistics approach and the elasticity of taxable income have reshaped public finance, connecting theory directly to administrative-data estimation and tax policy design. Impact on research and policy is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Chetty (sufficient statistics) and Saez (taxable income, optimal tax and top-income work) are the central figures. Slemrod and Stantcheva are important but the conceptual and empirical push came mainly from the first two. Saez's contributions overlap with the inequality candidate, and Chetty's with the mobility candidate.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work with substantial replication, though elasticity estimates and their policy interpretation remain contested.
uncertainties: Cross-candidate overlap in Chetty's and Saez's work complicates attribution and prize design.
The size of taxable-income elasticities and their welfare interpretation are debated.
Both laureates are comparatively young for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed trade theory and empirics and shifted the focus from industries and countries to firms. The framework gave new accounts of the gains from trade and has been used extensively.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman and co-authors made foundational extensions in firm-level and heterogeneity-based trade theory. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation and extension. It is a mature, widely taught framework.
uncertainties: Whether Helpman is best credited here or alongside Grossman for other work.
The 2008 prize already recognised new trade theory, which may shape the committee's appetite for another trade prize.
Gains-from-trade implications are sensitive to model specification.
